The Dream have called Gateway Center Arena in College Park home for the last six seasons, which only has a capacity of around 3,500. But the Dream have moved every playoff game this year to the much larger State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, an arena operated by the NBA's Hawks that holds a little more than 17,000. Once the WNBA Finals matchup was set, it wasn't clear where the league was going to hold the three games in Atlanta. The WNBA set the Finals schedule months in advance with national television partners, and State Farm Arena had conflicts for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6. But on Oct. 13 , the WNBA announced that Games 3 and 4, the two guaranteed-to-be-played games in Atlanta, would be moved in order to get them played in State Farm Arena. Left unsaid, though, was what would happen if the series went to the sixth game, which is currently scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 28. The league still hasn't answered that question by Saturday's tip time, but a Hawks executive has taken people inside the negotiations. Atlanta Hawks chief operating officer Steve Koonin went on 92.9 The Game, Atlanta's sports talk radio station on WZGC-FM, on the " Dukes and Bell " show on Friday and was asked about Game 6 and gave a rather ominous quote. item.title: Chris Sutton says Arsenal’s big squad has helped them again
item.description: Chris Sutton says Arsenal’s big squad has helped them again Chris Sutton has praised Arsenal’s squad depth after the Gunners defeated Everton , just days after Bukayo Saka suffered a long-term injury. The former striker believes Mikel Arteta has enough quality in his squad to cope with the winger’s absence and continue collecting important points. Saka has been one of Arsenal’s most influential players, so news that he would be sidelined for two months raised concerns among supporters. His creativity and attacking contributions have made him a key figure, leaving questions about how the team would perform without him. However, Arsenal have quality alternatives in several positions, giving Arteta options to adjust his starting eleven. Their first test following Saka’s injury came against Everton, providing an opportunity to show they could still deliver without one of their biggest stars. Arsenal demonstrate their squad depth David Moyes has beaten Arsenal several times during his managerial career and arrived in North London hoping to secure a positive result. However, the Gunners proved too strong, producing an assured performance to claim all three points. The victory demonstrated that Arsenal can remain competitive without Saka. Although replacing his quality is difficult, the squad has capable players who can help maintain the team’s standards during his absence. Sutton believes this strength in numbers played an important role in the result, allowing Arteta to make changes without significantly weakening his side. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Sutton praises Arsenal’s options Speaking via BBC Live , Sutton highlighted the importance of having reliable replacements available when key players are injured. “It’s about squad depth and Arsenal have shown today changes which they’ve made, with Bukayo Saka being injured and out for a while, but they have players who can come in and may not be as effective but still enough to get over the line. A big three points.” The victory offers encouragement to Arteta as he prepares for the coming fixtures. item.title: Chase Briscoe Wins Pole for Talladega’s YellaWood 500
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez Chase Briscoe delivered a strong qualifying performance on Saturday, securing the pole position for Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver put his No. 19 Toyota at the top of the leaderboard, earning a crucial starting position as the championship battle enters another important weekend. Briscoe posted a lap at 186.065 mph, completing the 2.66-mile superspeedway in 51.466 seconds. His effort narrowly edged Austin Hill, who qualified second with a speed of 185.949 mph. The difference between the two drivers was just 0.032 seconds, making it a close battle for the top starting spot. The pole marks Briscoe’s first of the 2026 season at Talladega and the 10th of his NASCAR Cup Series career. It also gives the No. 19 team another reason to feel confident heading into a race that could have significant championship implications. Briscoe has enjoyed success throughout the Chase, including victories at Las Vegas and Charlotte. He also enters the weekend as the defending winner of the fall Talladega race, giving him an opportunity to repeat that performance in front of the Alabama crowd. The Indiana native currently sits third in the championship standings, 24 points behind leader Kyle Larson. With only three races remaining, every stage point and finishing position could make a difference in determining who advances toward the championship. Starting up front does not guarantee success at Talladega, where drafting, aggressive moves and large multi-car accidents can dramatically change the race. However, Briscoe has positioned himself to take advantage of the opening laps and potentially collect valuable points early. Austin Hill will join Briscoe on the front row, while Trackhouse Racing teammates Connor Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen qualified third and fourth, respectively. Chris Buescher rounded out the top five. Several championship contenders will have more ground to make up. Larson qualified 10th, while Joey Logano will start 16th, Chase Elliott 18th and Ryan Blaney 27th. Tyler Reddick, who won at Phoenix last weekend, qualified 33rd. Sunday’s YellaWood 500 is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET on NBC. With the championship battle tightening, Briscoe will look to turn his pole position into another victory and close the gap on Larson in the standings.

The Detroit Lions (3-2) reportedly plan to activate star safety Brian Branch ahead of Sunday’s Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers (4-2) , setting up his long-awaited return from a torn Achilles. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler shared the development Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter, while reposting a hype video released by Detroit. “Lions plan to activate safety Brian Branch, who returns nearly 11 months from his Achilles tear. He’s set to make his season debut Sunday vs Packers,” Fowler wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Branch has been sidelined since suffering a torn Achilles during Detroit’s Week 14 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 4, 2025. The injury occurred while he attempted to break up a pass in the end zone. The 25-year-old subsequently missed the remainder of the 2025 campaign and began the 2026 season on the physically unable to perform list . Lions plan to activate safety Brian Branch, who returns nearly 11 months from his Achilles tear. He’s set to make his season debut Sunday vs Packers. pic.twitter.com/E72oKVcICd — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 24, 2026 Brian Branch’s return provides major boost to Lions’ secondary Before suffering the injury, Branch appeared in 12 games last season, recording 75 total tackles, including five tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, nine passes defended and one forced fumble. item.title: Naji Marshall Steps Up As Dallas Mavericks’ New Enforcer
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The most surprising thing about Naji Marshall’s Friday night performance wasn’t his 15 points or three steals. It was the fact that he ran from half court to confront a teammate’s attacker and picked up a technical for it. Marshall proved he is the physical shield the Dallas Mavericks need right now. He did not back down from a hard foul that left a young star injured on the floor. During the second quarter, Aaron Nesmith committed a rough foul while trying to block a dunk attempt by Cooper Flagg. Flagg was in mid-air and had no way to protect himself when Nesmith hit him. The impact caused Flagg to injure his left shoulder, the same one that troubled him last year. Marshall saw the play and immediately ran over to Nesmith to demand answers. The two players had to be pulled apart before the situation got worse. Both men received double technical fouls for the heated exchange. Defending the Team First Marshall is known for being protective of his teammates throughout his entire career. According to The Smoking Cuban , he is not a hothead who looks for fights, but he will not tolerate nonsense. He ran from the other side of the court to stand up for Flagg, who is seen as a young superstar for the franchise. Marshall is now fully adopting the enforcer role the Mavericks require from him, as this action demonstrates. He made it clear that no one goes after his friends without consequences. Although P.J. Washington possesses this protective quality as well, reports indicate Marshall could be an even stronger enforcer than Washington. The Smoking Cuban noted that Marshall is notoriously protective of teammates and that he isn’t going to let anyone hurt his friends. This mindset is crucial for a team that wants to win a championship. A squad needs players who will stand up for each other when the refs miss a call or a rival plays dirty. Marshall delivered that message loud and clear on Friday night. A Public Promise of Loyalty After the game, Marshall took to social media to show his loyalty to the team. He posted a message on X stating he would stand up for Flagg and anyone else wearing a Mavericks uniform. The post included a direct quote where he said, “I got you 32…any # on this side tbh!!!! #1stoneeeeeeeee LETS KEEP IT GOING MY BROTHASSSSS!!!!!!!!!!!” This public declaration reinforces the idea that he is the guy Dallas fans can trust to handle the physical side of the game. RotoWire reported that Marshall finished with 15 points and three steals in the 121-105 win over the Pacers. He played 33 minutes and helped secure the team’s first win of the season. The Mavericks now have a player who is ready to take a charge for his teammates. Marshall’s stats were solid, but his willingness to get into trouble for the team is what matters most. According to The Smoking Cuban, he got into Nesmith’s grill and likely exchanged some choice words with him. That kind of fire is rare to find in the modern NBA.

item.title: ‘I don’t think LeBron’s a total disgrace’: Skip Bayless defends LeBron James from President Trump
item.description: Skip Bayless has spent much of his career as one of LeBron James’ harshest critics. But when it comes to President Donald Trump’s latest attacks on the Philadelphia 76ers star, even Bayless is coming to James’ defense. In a conversation with Stephen A. Smith, Bayless pushed back on Trump calling James a “total disgrace” over his behavior during the national anthem. While Bayless called James “the ultimate diva,” he said that James has been “a very good role model” off the court, and suggested that Trump’s comments are about politics. Trump vs. LeBron Before the Sixers’ season opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday, video shared by ClutchPoints showed James swinging his arms as if practicing a golf swing during the national anthem, then going through his shooting motion. The moment drew backlash from conservative pundits, and on Thursday, Trump demanded an apology on Truth Social. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote. Later that day, Trump mocked James’ golf swing during a rally, calling it “a big scandal kind of a story.” James brushed off the criticism after the Sixers’ comeback win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night. “Must (have been) a slow news day at the office, you know? Slow news day in the office,” James said, via USA Today . ‘The Ultimate Diva’ Bayless, a longtime critic of LeBron, didn’t exactly let the NBA superstar off the hook for the moment itself as he called LeBron “the ultimate diva.” “I don’t think LeBron is deeply sort of psychologically wanting to protest the anthem. I think LeBron is, you know, he is the ultimate diva, and he’s earned a lot of his divaness,” Bayless said in a clip shared on X . “But he wants during the anthem to do a look at me. item.title: GAME THREAD: Washington State welcomes No. 21 Boise State for Homecoming
item.description: CORVALLIS, OR - OCTOBER 17: Players of the Washington State Cougars huddle during the first half of a game between the Washington State Cougars and the Oregon State Beavers at Reser Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Corvallis, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Good afternoon, Cougar football fans. It’s Homecoming weekend on the Palouse, and the Washington State Cougars face off with the No. 21 Boise State Broncos. WSU (1-6, 0-3 in Pac-12) began the second half of the 2026 season down in Corvallis, Oregon against the Oregon State Beavers last week and lost their fourth straight game, 48-30. In that game, WSU started a different quarterback, redshirt freshman Owen Eschelman. In his collegiate debut, Eschelman provided the Cougar offense a jolt that they desperately needed. In the last three prior games, WSU had scored just three offensive touchdowns. Against OSU, Eschelman had three himself. Two through the air and one rushing. He finished the game 32 for 49 in pass attempts for 289 passing yards and one interception that came very late in the game. He also had 15 total rushing attempts for another 136 yards. He will again get the start today. BSU (5-1, 2-0) is riding high off five straight wins and is off a bye week. In their last game two weeks ago, the Broncos defeated the Fresno State Bulldogs 38-31 in Fresno, California, to bring the Milk Can back to Boise for the first time since 2022. If WSU is going to pull off the upset, they will need Eschelman to continue to elevate the offense like he did last week. They will also need to find a way to efficiently run the football. Last week, Cougar running backs had 13 rushing attempts for 26 yards. That’s not going to cut it. Boise State’s run defense is vulnerable, though. The Broncos are giving up five yards per rush attempt on the season. What isn’t very vulnerable for the blue and orange has been their incredibly efficient offense. The Bronco offense won’t beat you over the top with many explosive plays, but they will grind their way down the field. They rank in the top 30 in success rate, power success, and stuff rate. The most telling stat for this Bronco offense is their time of possession. The Broncos lead FBS in time of possession percentage at 60.23%. WSU’s defense is going to have to find their way off the field early in Bronco possession, not just to prevent them from scoring, but to make sure they are too fatigued late in the game. Kickoff is at 3:00 p.m. and it couldn’t be a more perfect day for Cougar football in Pullman. It should be about a crisp 54 degrees at kickoff with very few clouds in sight and some slight wind. Go Cougs!

item.title: Couple Badgers starters on injury report, while USC has 6 players out, 3 questionable
item.description: Austin Kawecki #51 of the Wisconsin Badgers lines up over the football at the line of scrimmage against the Western Illinois Leathernecks at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin, on September 12, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are taking on the No. 16 USC Trojans at Camp Randall Stadium on Saturday night, looking to bounce back from their 17-7 loss to the No. 12 UCLA Bruins last weekend. The Badgers were on a four-game win streak going into last weekend and were expected to be fresh coming off their bye. The defense stood up to the challenge, stopping one of the best rushing attacks in the NCAA, but they did struggle to defend third downs in the passing game. USC, on the other hand, is coming off their bye week after an impressive 31-23 road win over Penn State, easing some of the tension from head coach Lincoln Riley. The Trojans are 6-1 this season, with their lone loss being to Oregon. But USC hasn’t been convincing in any of its recent wins, and they’re now heading on the road into another tough environment in Madison. Heading into Saturday, we’ve got a loaded injury report on both sides. For the Badgers, there are only five players with a ‘probable’ or ‘questionable’ diagnosis. Starters Javan Robinson, Darrion Dupree, and Austin Kawecki are probable, while running back Nate Palmer and wide receiver Malachi Coleman are questionable. Wisconsin opened the week with Robinson and Coleman as questionable. Robinson was finally upgraded to probable on Friday, while Coleman remains questionable. Kawecki has been probable all week. Dupree wasn’t on the injury report on Wednesday, but popped up on Thursday and Friday, although he was still listed as probable on both days. Palmer started the week as doubtful, but was upgraded to questionable on Thursday and Friday. USC’s side is more of an issue. The Trojans are without wideout Terrell Anderson, wideout Corey Simms, safety Kendarius Reddick, linebacker Taylor Johnson, linebacker Roman Marchetti, and Kilian O’Connor. Where things get more interesting is the questionable section, as tight end Mark Bowman, wideout Luc Weaver, and defensive tackle Jide Abasiri are all questionable for the game, while Jahkeem Stewart and Jaydn Walker are questionable. Getting Bowman, a five-star true freshman, back for the Trojans would be huge. Former Wisconsin transfer Tucker Ashcraft could be the starter if Bowman remains out, as he’s been the last two games. Elsewhere, Weaver saw an uptick in role with Anderson and Simms up for the season. He’s questionable. Abasiri is also a key cog for the Trojans up front. Stewart, a former five-star and another much-needed player for USC, should play on Saturday night.

Maryland dominated the paint in the first half, outscoring North Carolina in the paint, 20-8. The Terps also outrebounded North Carolina 23-18, allowing just one first-half offensive rebound. Head coach Brenda Frese said Agara needed to do a better job anchoring the defense after the Terps allowed 40 points in the paint and 18 offensive rebounds against Virginia Tech on Monday. Those numbers dropped to 26 and seven, respectively, on Saturday. Meanwhile, Jones flourished in the second half. The freshman made consecutive baskets at the beginning of the third quarter for her first points of the game, pushing Maryland ahead, 36-33. item.title: Former West Boca star Javian Mallory big part of offense in Canes' win
item.description: No. 1 ranked Miami defeated Pittsburgh 52-23 on Saturday afternoon at Hard Rock Stadium and Javian Mallory was once again a big part of the offensive explosion. While receiver Malachi Toney stole headlines with a career performance, Mallory, a former West Boca Raton High School standout running back, rushed for 47 yards and two touchdowns on seven carries for the 7-0 Canes. One of those scores was an 11-yard powerful run up the middle in which Mallory showcased a little Le'Veon-Bell-esque stutter-step before he hit the hole on his way to the end zone. TOUCHDOWN HURRICANES! 🔥 Javian gets it done on the ground 🙌 pic.twitter.com/V4uB0qYaSY — Miami Hurricanes Football (@CanesFootball) October 24, 2026 Mallory was an annual Palm Beach Post first-team All-County football selection and committed early to Miami. Thus far in his freshman season, he has 444 yards and seven scores. The performances against Pitt followed another two-touchdown performance on 108 yards rushing against FSU, a game that went to double overtime before UM won. He is the team's leading rusher through seven games. Miami played in the 2026 College Football Playoff National Championship game, losing to Indiana. Mallory was present in uniform, although he did not play. This year, he would be part of the team seeking to go one step farther. item.description: FILE PHOTO - German tennis player Jan-Lennard Struff reacts during his men's singles quarter-final match against Italy's Jannik Sinner on Day Nine of the 2026 Wimbledon Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. Kyle Shanahan shut down that idea on Thursday. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own-goal and Cole Palmer saw red after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
